title: Scientific Miracles in Ocean and Animals
author: Noted as unknown or various Islamic scholars (often attributed to Harun Yahya or similar authors, but title may represent a genre or pamphlet rather than a specific author)
publication_date: Varies (frequently published in the early 2000s, republished and distributed in print and online since then)
edition_analyzed: Standard widely-circulated English-language edition (exact publisher and year may vary)
target_audience: Muslim readers interested in signs of the divine in nature and science
General audiences curious about interconnections between religion and science
core_themes: Perceived miraculous aspects of the oceans and animals
Correlation between modern scientific discoveries and verses from the Qur’an
Arguing for the divine inspiration of Islamic scripture through natural phenomena
Wonder and awe at the complexity of the natural world
primary_purpose: To highlight and interpret select scientific facts about oceans and animals as evidence of the divine origin of the Qur’an, aiming to strengthen faith by demonstrating how modern discoveries are aligned with ancient scripture.

structure_format.organization: Thematic chapters or sections focusing on specific animals, oceanic phenomena, or Qur’anic verses
features: Descriptions and facts about animals and marine science
Comparisons of scriptural references and scientific findings

key_concepts_lessons: Certain verses in the Qur’an are said to reference scientific phenomena unknown at the time of revelation, such as oceanic currents, the darkness of deep seas, or the honeybee’s behavior.
The intricate design of animals and their behaviors serve as signs of a Creator’s wisdom.
Scientific understanding can be harmonized with religious belief and can serve to reinforce faith.
Studying nature can be viewed as a form of appreciating or worshipping the Creator.
notable_features: Blending of scientific information with scriptural exegesis
Use of contemporary scientific discoveries to support timeless religious claims
cultural_historical_context: Books and pamphlets in this genre grew in popularity in the late 20th and early 21st centuries, particularly among Muslim audiences experiencing renewed interest in harmonizing scientific progress with traditional beliefs, and in response to global discussions about science and religion.
reception_impact: Widely circulated in Muslim communities and at interfaith gatherings
Credited with strengthening belief among lay readers and youth
Criticized by some scientists and skeptics for selective interpretation and confirmation bias
Has inspired further interest in exploring scientific topics within religious frameworks
comparable_titles: The Miracles of the Qur’an by Harun Yahya
The Bible, The Qur’an and Science by Dr. Maurice Bucaille
